extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners (attorneys/agents/applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Form paragraphs and examiner guidance from the MPEP for making and explaining rejections of design patent claims under various provisions of 35 U.S.C. (pre‑AIA and AIA) including 102, 103 and related procedural notices; includes suggested ways to overcome rejections and bracket insertion instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.12.fti Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(b) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(b) as being anticipated by [1] because the invention was patented or described in a printed publication in this or a foreign country, or in public use or on sale in this country more than one (1) year prior to the application for patent in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph should be used in any application filed on or after March 16, 2013, that is subject to the pre‑AIA prior art provisions. Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design. For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.10.15 Notice re prior art available under both pre-AIA and AIA
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice that if the determination of the status of the application as subject to AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 (or as subject to pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103) is incorrect, any correction of the statutory basis for the rejection will not be considered a new ground of rejection if the prior art relied upon, and the rationale supporting the rejection, would be the same under either status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design. For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 15.10.15 (i.e., this paragraph often precedes or accompanies other paragraphs to notify of dual‑status prior art).

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.13.fti Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(c) because the invention has been abandoned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this form paragraph in all Office Actions when a prior art rejection is made in an application with an abandoned prior application or other factual basis for 102(c). Examiner Note: (In bracket 1, identify reference as needed.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.14.fti Pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d)/35 U.S.C. 172 Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(d), as modified by pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 172, as being anticipated by [1] because the invention was first patented or caused to be patented, or was the subject of an inventor’s certificate by the applicant, or his/her legal representatives or assigns in a foreign country prior to the date of the application for patent in this country on an application for patent or inventor’s certificate filed more than six (6) months before the filing of the application in the United States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design and include appropriate citation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.aia 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by [1] because the claimed invention was described in a patent issued under section 151, or in an application for patent published or deemed published under section 122(b), in which the patent or application, as the case may be, names another inventor and was effectively filed before the effective filing date of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference. For applications claiming priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15. This paragraph should only be used in an application filed on or after March 16, 2013, and where claims are examined under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 as amended by the AIA.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by [1] because the invention was described in a patented or published application for patent by another filed in the United States before the invention thereof by the applicant for patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design. For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013, that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.01.aia Explanation of rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1) or 102(a)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appearance of [1] is substantially the same as that of the claimed design.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this paragraph after 15.11.aia or 15.15.aia to explain the basis of the rejection. Cites International Seaway Trading Corp. v. Walgreens Corp., and MPEP § 1504.02. Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.01.fti Explanation of rejection under Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(a), (b), (d), or (e)
rubrics_metrics.description: The appearance of [1] is substantially the same as that of the claimed design (analogous explanation for pre‑AIA statutory grounds).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This paragraph should be included after paragraph 15.11.fti, 15.12.fti, 15.14.fti or 15.15.fti to explain the basis of the rejection. For applications with actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to an earlier application, precede with form paragraph 15.10.15. Examiner Note: In bracket 1, identify the reference applied against the claimed design.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.02.aia 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) Provisional rejection - design disclosed in another application with common inventor and/or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [1] which has a common [2] with the instant application. Because the copending application names another inventor and has an earlier effective filing date, it would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published under 122(b) or patented. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provisional rejection might be overcome by: (1) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the design in the reference was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor of this application (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119 by filing certified priority document satisfying 35 U.S.C. 112(a); (3) perfecting the benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 by filing an application data sheet under 37 CFR 1.76 with specific reference per 1.78 and establishing enablement/description under 112(a); (4) a showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(B); or (5) providing a statement under 35 U.S.C. 102(b)(2)(C) that subject matter and claimed invention were owned by same person or subject to assignment/joint research agreement. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Examiner Notes: Used to provisionally reject over copending application (utility or design) with earlier filing date that discloses the claimed invention; copending application must have either common assignee or at least one common inventor. In bracket 2 insert 'inventor' or 'assignee'. For certain priority situations precede with paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.02.fti Provisional Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection - design disclosed but not claimed in another application with common inventor and/or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by copending Application No. [1] which has a common [2] with the instant application. Based upon the different inventive entity and the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), if published under 122(b) or patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested ways to overcome: (A) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the design in the reference was derived from the designer of this application (thus not 'by another'); (B) showing a date of invention for the instant application prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); (C) perfecting a claim to priority under 35 U.S.C. 119 by filing certified priority document meeting 112(a) requirements; (D) perfecting benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 per 37 CFR 1.78 and establishing enablement/description. Administrative notes: If application filed before Sept 16, 2012 include specific reference in first sentences of specification or in ADS; if on/after Sept16,2012 include in ADS. Use pre‑AIA 102(e) as amended by AIPA to determine reference's prior art date unless reference is US patent issued from int'l app with filing date prior to Nov 29, 2000; otherwise use pre‑AIPA 102(e). Examiner Notes: In bracket 2 insert inventor or assignee. For certain priority situations precede with paragraph 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.03.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) provisional rejection - design claimed in an earlier‑filed design patent application with common inventor and/or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as being anticipated by the claim in copending Design Patent Application No. [1] which has a common [2] with the instant application. Based upon the different inventive entity and the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if patented. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future patenting of the copending application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rejection may be overcome by abandoning the earlier‑filed copending application. Examiner Note: In bracket 2 insert inventor or assignee. This form paragraph must be preceded by 15.24.05.fti to notify applicant that the question of patentability under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f)/(g) also exists. For certain priority situations precede with 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.04.aia 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) rejection - design disclosed in a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as being anticipated by patent [1]. Because the patent names another inventor and has an earlier effective filing date, it constitutes prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that disclosure in the reference was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor of this application (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119 by filing certified priority documents meeting 112(a); (3) perfecting benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 via ADS per 37 CFR 1.76 and 1.78; (4) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (5) providing statement under 102(b)(2)(C) of common ownership/assignment/joint research. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Examiner Note: Use when claimed design is disclosed in the drawings of an earlier‑filed design or utility patent; insert patent number in bracket 1. For certain priority situations precede with 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.15.04.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) rejection - design disclosed but not claimed in a patent
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 as being anticipated by patent [1]. Based upon the different inventive entity and the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the reference, it constitutes prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the design claimed in the present application is not the same invention claimed in patent [2], suggested ways to overcome include: (A) showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the design in the reference was derived from the designer of this application and is thus not 'by another'; (B) showing a date of invention for the instant application prior to the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a); (C) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119; or (D) perfecting benefit claim under 35 U.S.C. 120 and establishing enablement/description. If application filed before Sept 16, 2012 include specific reference in spec or ADS; if filed on/after Sept 16, 2012 include in ADS. This rejection may not be overcome by filing a terminal disclaimer (In re Bartfeld). Examiner Note: Use when claimed design is disclosed in drawings of earlier‑filed design or utility patent but not claimed therein.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.16.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 because applicant did not himself invent the subject matter sought to be patented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use where factual showing supports that the named applicant is not the actual inventor. (No additional bracket instructions in the excerpt.)

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.17.aia Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102 because, before the applicant’s invention thereof, the invention was made in this country by another who had not abandoned, suppressed or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rejection based on this statutory basis can be made in an application or patent that is examined under the first‑to‑file provisions of the AIA if it also contains or contained at any time (1) a claim to an invention having an effective filing date as defined in 35 U.S.C. 100(i) that is before March 16, 2013, or (2) a specific reference under 35 U.S.C. 120, 121, or 365(c) to any patent or application that contains or contained at any time such a claim. Examiner Note: For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.17.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) Rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(g) because, before the applicant’s invention thereof, the invention was made in this country by another who had not abandoned, suppressed or concealed it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 15.10.fti and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.18.aia 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (Single Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [1]. Although the invention is not identically disclosed or described as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date of the claimed invention to a designer having ordinary skill in the art to which the claimed invention pertains, the invention is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: In bracket 1, insert the reference citation. For applications claiming priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.aia 35 U.S.C. 103 Rejection (Multiple Reference)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over [1] in view of [2]. Although the invention is not identically disclosed or described as set forth in 35 U.S.C. 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious before the effective filing date to a designer having ordinary skill in the art, the invention is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: For applications claiming priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraphs 15.10.aia and 15.10.15. In brackets insert appropriate reference citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.fti Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) Rejection (Multiple References)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being unpatentable over [1] in view of [2]. If differences between the subject matter sought to be patented and the prior art are such that the subject matter as a whole would have been obvious at the time the invention was made to a designer of ordinary skill in the art, the invention is not patentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: For applications with an actual filing date on or after March 16, 2013 that claim priority to, or the benefit of, an application filed before March 16, 2013, this form paragraph must be preceded by form paragraph 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.01 Summary Statement of Rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim stands rejected under [1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use as a summary statement of rejection(s) in an Office action. In bracket 1 insert appropriate basis for rejection (statutory provisions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.02.aia Preface 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)/103 rejection - Different inventors, common assignee, obvious designs, no evidence of common ownership not later than effective filing date of claimed design
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is directed to a design not patentably distinct from the design of commonly assigned [1]. Specifically, the claimed design is different from the one in [2] in that [3]. These differences are considered obvious and do not patentably distinguish the overall appearance of the claimed design over the design in [4]. The commonly assigned [5] names another inventor and was effectively filed before the present application and thus qualifies as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rejection might be overcome by: (1) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(a) that the design in the reference was obtained directly or indirectly from the inventor or a joint inventor (not prior art under 102(b)(2)(A)); (2) perfecting priority under 35 U.S.C. 119; (3) perfecting benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120 via ADS and 1.78; (4) showing under 37 CFR 1.130(b) of a prior public disclosure under 102(b)(2)(B); or (5) providing a statement under 102(b)(2)(C) that the designs were owned by the same person or subject to assignment/joint research agreement as of the effective filing date. Examiner Notes: An obviousness double patenting rejection may also be included. In brackets insert 'patent' and number, or 'copending application' and serial number as appropriate. In bracket 3 identify differences. This paragraph should only be used ONCE in an Office action and for certain priority situations precede with 15.10.aia and 15.10.15.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.02.fti Preface pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection - Different inventors, common assignee, obvious designs, no evidence of common ownership at time later design was made
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is directed to a design not patentably distinct from the design of commonly assigned [1]. Specifically, the claimed design is different from the one in [2] in that [3]. These differences are considered obvious and do not patentably distinguish the overall appearance of the claimed design over the design in [4]. The commonly assigned [5] has a different inventive entity and therefore qualifies as prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) and forms the basis for rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) if the conflicting design claims were not commonly owned at the time the design in this application was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant/assignee/attorney can resolve by stating that conflicting designs were commonly owned at the time the design in this application was made, or the assignee can name the prior inventor of the conflicting subject matter. A showing of common ownership at the relevant time will overcome a rejection under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) based upon the commonly assigned case as a reference under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(f) or 102(g), or pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) for apps filed on/after Nov 29, 1999. Examiner Notes: Use when commonly assigned but no indication of common assignment at time invention was made. If conflicting claim is in a patent with earlier US filing date, make 102(e)/103(a) rejection. If in commonly assigned copending application with earlier filing date, provisionally reject under pre‑AIA 102(e)/103(a). An obviousness double patenting rejection may also be included. Insert patent/copending application numbers in brackets and identify differences in bracket 3. This paragraph should only be used ONCE in an Office action. For determining reference's pre‑AIA or pre‑AIPA 102(e) date follow guidance in paragraphs 7.12.fti / 7.12.01.fti.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.03.aia 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2)/103 Provisional Rejection - design disclosed in another application with common inventor and/or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is provisionally rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being obvious over copending Application No. [1] which has a common [2] with the instant application. Because the copending application names another inventor and has an earlier effective filing date, it would constitute prior art under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) if published under 122(b) or patented. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the conflicting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not identically disclosed under 102, if the differences between the claimed invention and the prior art are such that the claimed invention as a whole would have been obvious to a person having ordinary skill in the art, the invention is not patentable. This provisional rejection might be overcome by the same remedies listed for provisional 102(a)(2) rejections (37 CFR 1.130(a)/(b), priority under 119, benefit under 120, statement under 102(b)(2)(C), etc.). Examiner Notes: Use when claimed design is obvious over subject matter disclosed in drawings of earlier‑filed design or utility application (may be broken lines or subcombinations). In brackets insert serial number of copending application and inventor/assignee as required; provide explanation of obviousness including differences in bracket 3; precede with 15.10.15 for certain priority situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: 15.19.03.fti Provisional Pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e)/103(a) rejection - design disclosed but not claimed in another application with common inventor and/or assignee
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim is provisionally rejected under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 103(a) as being obvious over copending Application No. [1] which has a common [2] with the instant application. Based upon the different inventive entity and the earlier effective U.S. filing date of the copending application, it would constitute prior art under pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) if published under 122(b) or patented. This provisional rejection is based upon a presumption of future publication or patenting of the conflicting application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since the design claimed in the present application is not the same invention claimed in the [4] application, this provisional rejection may be overcome by a showing under 37 CFR 1.132 that the design in the reference was derived from the designer of this application and is thus not 'by another,' or by a showing of a date of invention for the instant application prior to the effective U.S. filing date of the reference under 37 CFR 1.131(a). For applications filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, this rejection might also be overcome by showing that the subject matter of the reference and the claimed invention were, at the time the invention was made, owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment to the same person. Alternatively, merging the two applications into a single continuation‑in‑part and abandoning the separate parent applications may overcome the rejection. Examiner Notes: In brackets insert serial number of copending application and inventor/assignee. Provide explanation of obviousness/differences in bracket 3 and follow explanation with form paragraphs 15.70.fti and 15.67 or 15.68 as applicable. Use pre‑AIA 35 U.S.C. 102(e) as amended by AIPA to determine reference's prior art date unless special exceptions apply. For certain priority situations precede with 15.10.15.
